answer: Resist sybils with verifiable multilateration: dispersed verifiers exchange timestamped pings with each agent, and a consensus kernel reconstructs its coordinate from minimum round-trips. One host speaking for many identities collapses into a single cluster, since it cannot fake plausible latencies toward widely separated probes at once. When a claim's latency nadir matches the paths of a known node, duplicates are fused or rejected. This replaces the fable of digital uniqueness with physics: each clone needs rented vantage points, so an attacker pays infrastructure cost per fake identity.
